title.narrative: Output 2.3. Increased capacity of Member States to engage in a forward-looking international labour standards policy

description.narrative: In November 2022, the statutory tripartite body, the National Advisory Committee on Labour endorsed the Draft Labour Bill which awaits adoption by the national authorities. The tripartite Committee has facilitated engagement on the integration of international labour standards as well as the CEACR. During the biennium as well as other biennia, the ILO has continued to provide technical and advisory support to the National Tripartite Task on the Labour Law Reform towards the finalization of the review of the national Labour Bill.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and Employment, in consultation with social partners started developing in 2023 occupational safety and health regulations for the agricultural sector. The aim is to prevent accidents and injuries arising out of, in connection with or in the course of work, by eliminating, minimizing or controlling hazards in the agricultural working environment. During the biennium, through awareness raising and capacity building interventions on OSH, the ILO provided support to constituents to draft the Regulations.

description.narrative: in March 2023, the Government deposited the instruments of ratification of ILO Conventions C/151, C/187 and C.190 During the biennium, through awareness raising and capacity building interventions, the ILO provided support to the ratification process, through support for tripartite consultations and enhanced capacity of constituents to understand and engage with the national authorities on the implications of ratification of the respective ILO Conventions.
